actions.action_title: Pass the Critical Mineral Dominance Act
caveats: The vote was on the House stage, not enactment.
Project acceleration and studies are distinct mechanisms within one bill.
actions.exact_stage: House passage of the committee substitute considered adopted under the rule
actions.mechanism: statutory agency direction, reporting, project prioritization, and permitting review

opponent_argument.text: Dissenting views disputed codifying the executive-order approach and raised environmental-review and public-land concerns.

actions.prior_baseline: Executive orders directed agencies on mineral production; the reported bill proposed statutory duties and studies.
actions.proposed_change: Codify selected mineral-production directives, require import-reliance reporting, identify and expedite priority projects, review impediments, and accelerate geologic mapping.
actions.scale: national federal mineral policy and federal lands

supporter_argument.text: The committee majority argued the bill would expand domestic mineral production and address supply-chain vulnerabilities.

actions.timing: ongoing duties and recurring reports after enactment

actions.action_title: Pass the Securing America's Critical Minerals Supply Act
caveats: The bill's defined resource category is broader than mineral names in the short title.
The vote does not establish support for every possible resource strategy.
actions.exact_stage: House passage of the amended bill
actions.mechanism: departmental mission, supply-chain assessment, strategy development, and congressional reporting

opponent_argument.text: Minority views argued the broad critical-energy-resource definition could include fossil resources and did not prioritize clean-energy supply chains.

actions.prior_baseline: DOE's organizing statute did not contain the bill's proposed critical-energy-resource functions and recurring assessments.
actions.proposed_change: Define critical energy resources, add DOE supply-security functions, require ongoing vulnerability assessments, develop diversification and domestic-production strategies, and report to Congress.

supporter_argument.text: The committee majority argued a durable DOE role was needed to assess vulnerabilities and strengthen critical-resource supply chains.

actions.timing: ongoing assessments and a report within two years

actions.action_title: Pass the Don't Mess With My Home Appliances Act
caveats: The bill changes a rulemaking framework; it does not itself set one appliance's efficiency level.
Existing distribution-transformer standards were not repealed by the described prohibition.
actions.exact_stage: House passage of the reported amended bill
actions.mechanism: statutory constraints on federal efficiency rulemaking

opponent_argument.text: Minority views argued the bill would add duplicative hurdles, weaken efficiency standards, and raise energy costs.

actions.prior_baseline: The Energy Policy and Conservation Act required recurring review and supplied existing criteria for appliance-efficiency standards.
actions.proposed_change: Revise DOE's standard-setting process, add savings and product-performance criteria, allow specified amendment or revocation, and bar new standards for distribution transformers.
actions.scale: federal standards for covered consumer products and commercial equipment

supporter_argument.text: The committee majority argued the additional criteria would protect product choice, performance, and affordability.

actions.timing: future and amended standards after enactment

actions.action_title: Pass the Homeowner Energy Freedom Act
caveats: The bill combines three program repeals.
Some contractor-training balances had already been rescinded under separate law.
Do not treat the vote as a view on every appliance or building code.
actions.exact_stage: House passage of the reported bill
actions.mechanism: program repeal and rescission of unobligated funds

opponent_argument.text: Minority views argued the programs reduced upgrade costs, supported workforce training, and helped lower energy use and bills.

actions.prior_baseline: Federal law authorized home-electrification rebates, contractor training grants, and grants for updated or zero-energy building-code adoption.
actions.proposed_change: Repeal those three programs and rescind specified unobligated balances.
actions.scale: three federal home-energy and building-code programs

supporter_argument.text: The committee majority argued repeal would preserve consumer choice and avoid federal pressure toward electrification and building-code adoption.

actions.timing: upon enactment, subject to remaining unobligated balances

actions.action_title: Pass the Protecting Access for Hunters and Anglers Act
caveats: The reported substitute retained a unit-specific exception.
The vote concerns federal lands and waters, not a nationwide ban on state regulation.
actions.exact_stage: House passage of the reported substitute
actions.mechanism: statutory limit on agency regulatory authority with an evidence-based exception

opponent_argument.text: Dissenting views argued the restriction would impede federal land managers' ability to address wildlife harms from lead.

actions.prior_baseline: Federal land-management agencies could regulate lead ammunition and tackle under existing authorities.
actions.proposed_change: Generally bar Interior and Agriculture land agencies from prohibiting or regulating lead ammunition or tackle on covered federal lands and waters, with a unit-specific wildlife exception.
actions.scale: covered federal lands and waters open to hunting or fishing

supporter_argument.text: The committee majority argued broad lead restrictions could reduce hunting and fishing access and should require unit-specific evidence.

actions.timing: after enactment; unit-specific exceptions require findings and notice
